_method_note: MEMBERSHIP IS BY NAME PREFIX (''), not by evidence. A function is in this ledger because someone once called it AI, and drops out the moment it is renamed -- so a misnamed function is silently in, and correcting the name silently removes it along with any progress recorded against it. See _reclassified_out for rows removed that way, and re-read a row's `callers_in_ai` before trusting its membership: a row with callers_in_ai 0 AND reachable_from_root false is only in this file on the strength of its name. Reachability here is UNCUT: a plain BFS from the root over the whole call graph. docs/ai-closure.md cut the BFS at ui/view edges (to keep the closure from swallowing render/audio at 779 functions), so it reports 155 ai-prefixed functions reachable and 63 not. This file reports more reachable (164) and fewer orphans because a path THROUGH a ui function still makes an AI function reachable -- the right test for 'does this need a caller-side hook', which is what batch E turns on. The two are not in conflict; they answer different questions. Layering is computed on AI-only edges, because only AI functions are ever armed and only they can nest with each other.

functions.name: llm_wait_screen_frame
functions.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-01. Translated in libmh/lockstep/net_session.cpp; its resync-completion transition is `resync_complete_local`, which rx_dispatch's CTL_RESYNC_END arm now calls too -- one implementation for the leader and the peer, which is what this item was opened for. Evidence: `net_selftest netsessiontest` covers all three branches (not leader / leader-below-deadline / leader-past-deadline), the JBE boundary from BOTH sides, the UNSIGNED compare across the GetTickCount wrap (deadline 0xFFFFFFF0, ticks 0x10 -- a signed reading acts, ours does not), the short circuit (a non-leader frame reads the clock ZERO times), and the act ORDER with mocks that sample the state they run under; `net_selftest lockstest` drives the leader path and the peer path over one world fixture and asserts an identical (STATUS_FLAGS, RESYNC_IN_PROGRESS) end state and the same three local acts. Mutation-tested: breaking the shared transition goes red on BOTH ends, which is what shows the RX arm routes through it rather than agreeing by coincidence. NOT shadow-armed: the body SENDS a CTL_RESYNC_END packet and DRAINS the socket, neither of which a state restore can undo. T2 rather than T1 because no available scenario drives a real leader-side resync to completion -- that needs a genuine stall -- so there is no live equivalence evidence for this body, only for the peer end of the same transition, which real MP runs exercise.

functions.name: llm_net_session_globals_reset
functions.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-01. Translated in libmh/lockstep/net_session.cpp, promoted into the `[promote] lockstep` closure. Evidence, two independent kinds. OFFLINE: `net_selftest netsessiontest` asserts all 22 stores against the values the listing stores (0x0049e4db..0x0049e5e9), the four doubles as BIT PATTERNS (0x4024000000000000 = 10.0, 0x4051800000000000 = 70.0, 0x3ff0.. = 1.0, 0xbff0.. = -1.0), plus idempotence; three mutations were each caught by the assertion that names them. LIVE: the read-back probe (seams/net_session_probe.cpp) at llm_net_init_stub -- the instruction after this function's call site -- reported `22/22 fields match, 0 mismatch` in BOTH arms: promoted (promote_lockstep=1, ours_calls=1, so OUR body wrote them) and stock (promote_lockstep=0, ours_calls=0, so the ORIGINAL did, which is what proves the address table rather than our own pointers). Negative arm: writing ADAPT_NEXT_TIME as 71.0 made the promoted run report `MISMATCH STRAT_LOCKSTEP_ADAPT_NEXT_TIME @0x005d55c4 = 0x4051c00000000000, want 0x4051800000000000` and 21/22. NOT shadow-armed and never will be: one call per process, so there is no second call to compare against.
